---
title: "Adjunctive echinocandin for HIV-negative Pneumocystis pneumonia"
---

## Overview

This site presents an interim **Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis** of adjunctive
echinocandin/caspofungin plus trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) versus TMP-SMX
monotherapy for all-cause mortality in HIV-negative / immunocompromised adults with
*Pneumocystis jirovecii* pneumonia (PCP/PJP). It corresponds to the PROSPERO-registered
review question on combination and adjunctive treatment regimens.

The full methods, results, figures, and reproducible code are on the
[Analysis & Results](pcp_echinocandin_meta_writeup.qmd) page.

## Headline finding

The verified evidence base is small and observational. Pooling the six source-verified
studies, adjunctive echinocandin shows a **possible but inconclusive** mortality benefit
versus monotherapy — the credible interval includes no effect:

| Analysis | Studies | Pooled OR (95% CrI) |
|---|---|---|
| Primary (in-hospital / ~30-day) | 3 | 0.78 (0.31–1.93) |
| Sensitivity (+ longer timepoints) | 6 | 0.76 (0.43–1.37) |

An OR below 1 favours combination therapy. The estimate is robust to prior choice but
sensitive to a single influential study (Xu2025); see the
[robustness checks](pcp_echinocandin_meta_writeup.qmd#robustness-leave-one-out).

## What was verified

- **Tian2020 excluded** — an HIV-positive cohort that had been misclassified in the
  machine-draft extraction.
- **Qi2025 / Yanmeng2026 de-duplicated** — the same PUMCH cohort; the full-cohort
  comparison (not the ventilated subgroup) was used.
- **Counts source-checked** against the original full texts for every included study.
